rationale: The claim is a study-bound empirical association: a recurrent network trained on simulated reaching develops internal population activity that predicts recorded motor-neuron firing. It is compatible with the established population-coding meta-principle, because both the model units and the recorded neurons are distributed populations whose joint activity can encode movement-related variables. The link is one of consistency rather than derivation: population coding does not by itself predict that an RNN trained on muscle dynamics will match neural firing, but the finding is a concrete instance of distributed population representation. The claim is also appropriately bounded by the mechanism-prediction distinction: predictive correspondence between model internal activity and neural firing does not establish that the brain implements the same recurrent mechanism. These links respect the study-bound scale and the empirical-association epistemic type of the principle.
